title.value: Variance Penalized On-Policy and Off-Policy Actor-Critic
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Variance Penalized On-Policy and Off-Policy Actor-Critic

analysis.description: The paper introduces on-policy and off-policy actor-critic algorithms that aim to optimize a performance criterion involving both mean and variance in the return. It proposes using a direct variance estimator for learning policies with less variability, showing convergence to locally optimal policies in finite state Markov decision processes. The empirical results demonstrate the algorithm's utility in different domains, emphasizing its ability to maintain expected returns while reducing return variance.

type.justification: The paper includes empirical analysis and experiments to demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm in different environments, such as tabular and continuous MuJoCo domains.
type.quote: We demonstrate the utility of our algorithm in tabular and continuous MuJoCo domains.

name.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning algorithms specifically targeting the policy optimization domain with regards to mean and variance in returns.
name.quote: Reinforcement learning algorithms are typically geared towards optimizing the expected return of an agent.

name.justification: The paper discusses optimizing algorithms by modifying the standard policy gradient objective to include variance adjustments for learning policies with lower variability.
name.quote: We modify the standard policy gradient objective to include a direct variance estimator for learning policies that maximize the variance-penalized return.

name.justification: The paper emphasizes using a direct variance estimation approach as opposed to traditional methods which involve estimating using second moments.
name.quote: Instead, we use a much simpler recently proposed direct variance estimator which updates the estimates incrementally using temporal difference methods.

name.justification: The VPAC algorithm is specifically discussed as a newly proposed model aimed at reducing the return variance while maintaining expected returns.
name.quote: We develop a multi-timescale actor-critic algorithm, by deriving the gradient of the variance estimator in both the on-policy and the off-policy case.
